metadata.name: [GCP Cloud SQL PostgreSQL OTel] HA failover occurred or standby unavailable
metadata.description: Alerts when a high-availability (regional) PostgreSQL instance requested an automatic failover in the last 15 minutes, or its latest available_for_failover sample is 0 (the standby cannot take over), for 2 consecutive checks. Optional metrics: both are reported only for HA instances, so zonal instances never alert. Applies the PostgreSQL engine marker. Grouped by database_id.

query.base:
TS metrics-gcp.cloudsql_postgresql.otel-*
| WHERE gcp.resource_type == "cloudsql_database"
// Resolve per minute first (fragmentation-safe).
// available_for_failover (GAUGE, >0 = standby ready) and auto_failover_request_count
// (DELTA) are reported only for HA (regional) instances; zonal instances never alert.
| STATS failover_ready = MAX(MAX_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/available_for_failover`)),
        failovers = SUM(SUM_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/auto_failover_request_count`)),
        pg = SUM(COUNT_OVER_TIME(`cloudsql.googleapis.com/database/postgresql/num_backends`))
    BY `@timestamp` = TBUCKET(1 minute), database_id
// PostgreSQL engine marker: excludes MySQL / SQL Server HA instances
| INLINE STATS pg_total = SUM(pg) BY database_id
| WHERE pg_total > 0 AND (failover_ready IS NOT NULL OR failovers IS NOT NULL)
| EVAL ready_ts = CASE(failover_ready IS NOT NULL, `@timestamp`, NULL)
| STATS failover_ready = LAST(failover_ready, ready_ts),
        ready_minutes = COUNT(failover_ready),
        failovers = SUM(failovers)
    BY database_id
| EVAL failovers = COALESCE(failovers, 0)

breach.segment:
// Breach when either:
//  - an automatic failover was requested in the window (the primary failed over), or
//  - the latest readiness sample says the standby cannot take over (HA protection lost).
WHERE failovers > 0 OR (ready_minutes > 0 AND failover_ready == 0)
| EVAL reason = CASE(
    failovers > 0 AND failover_ready == 0, "automatic failover occurred; standby not ready",
    failovers > 0, "automatic failover occurred",
    "standby not available for failover")
| KEEP database_id, reason, failovers, failover_ready
| SORT database_id
| LIMIT 100

data.content:
## Cloud SQL PostgreSQL HA failover occurred or standby unavailable

Either the primary failed over to its standby, or the instance has lost its ability to fail over.

### Triage
1. `automatic failover occurred`: the primary zone or VM failed. Check the Cloud SQL operations log and Google Cloud status for the region. Clients reconnect to the same IP; verify application error rates and connection storms after the event.
2. `standby not available for failover`: HA protection is lost. This is expected briefly during maintenance or right after a failover while the standby is rebuilt. If it persists, check the operations log and open a support case.
3. Check the instance down and restarted alerts for the same instance.

### Tuning
- Increase the alert delay if maintenance regularly causes short readiness gaps.
